cultural.vision_reason: A hand-woven strip cotton textile with black-and-white geometric supplementary-weft patterning, consistent with traditional Guinea-Bissau strip weaving practices attributed to the Papel.

physical.title: textile
physical.summary:
Textile consisting of six narrow strip woven cotton lengths, hand sewn together selvedge to selvedge. Ground weave: plain weave: white and dyed black warps and wefts. This creates a cloth with a white background with bands of weft stripes at either end in black. The cloth is then decorated using supplementary weft and supplementary weft floats. There is a broad weft band at each end of the textile consisting of two distinct patterns, one based in the diamond shape the other based on triangles. The central panel is divided into warp stripes by lines in black supplementary weft. Within each of these stripes there are clusters of diamonds and clusters of diamonds and triangles which are broken by lines in the weft direction at regular intervals. 

The cloth is finished by unworked warps.
